messages.body_plain:
Dr. Karl,

After loading in the genotype data set into R with read.cross(), I am trying to figure out what is the best way to map the markers for an F2 intercross. I followed the manual for genetic map construction with R/qtl, and tried these functions:

> lg <- formLinkageGroups(mapthis, max.rf=0.35, min.lod=6)
> table(lg[,2])

but when I plot
> plotRF(mapthis, alternate.chrid=TRUE)
to see how well it worked, the plot is not anywhere close to the example plot in the manual.

Here is my code (I tried ordering markers on chromosome 5):

> lg <- formLinkageGroups(map_athaf, max.rf=0.35, min.lod=13)
Warning message:
In formLinkageGroups(map_athaf, max.rf = 0.35, min.lod = 13) :
  Running est.rf.
> table(lg[,2])

  1   2   3   4   5
207 106  97  85   4

> map_athaf_lg <- formLinkageGroups(map_athaf, max.rf=0.35, min.lod=13, reorgMarkers=TRUE)
Warning message:
In formLinkageGroups(map_athaf, max.rf = 0.35, min.lod = 13, reorgMarkers = TRUE) :
  Running est.rf.
> plotRF(map_athaf_lg, alternate.chrid=TRUE)
> map_athaf_chr5 <- orderMarkers(map_athaf_lg, chr=5)
> pull.map(map_athaf_chr5, chr=5)
 30.1_CHR_5_544767 30.1_CHR_5_1283613 30.1_CHR_5_1283633 30.1_CHR_5_1297106
         0.0000000          0.4163351          0.4163486          0.4163621

I then came across another discussion on the google group, and I wondered whether I should be doing this:

#####################
#### listeria data, pretending we don't know chr assignments or marker order
# load listeria data
data(listeria)

# omit the X chromosome
listeria <- subset(listeria, chr="-X")

# markers not on chr 1
mnames <- markernames(listeria, chr="-1")

# move them to chr 1
for(i in mnames)
  listeria <- movemarker(listeria, i, 1)

# randomize marker order
listeria <- switch.order(listeria, chr=1, order=sample(totmar(listeria)))

#### estimate pairwise recombination fractions
listeria <- est.rf(listeria)
plot.rf(listeria)

#### establish linkage groups
revlisteria <- formLinkageGroups(listeria, reorgMarkers=TRUE)
plot.rf(revlisteria)

#### determine marker order on each chromosome
revlisteria <- orderMarkers(revlisteria, verbose=TRUE)
plot.rf(revlisteria)
#####################

What would be the best way to go about ordering the markers? Thank you so much for your help!

formLinkageGroups() will just assign markers to linkage groups, but
without attempting to order them.
orderMarkers() attempts to order the markers on each chromosome, but it
should be followed up with ripple() and close inspection of the plotRF()
plot.

karl

Hi SAMBOU

I’m sorry for jumping too quickly to find the solution for you without asking for further information from the experimental design.

I think I might misunderstand the definition of BC2F4 population.

I’m working with crops and mostly they are self-pollinate and diploid.

So, I think the BC2F4 population might from F1 which generated from two parent, P1 and P2, in line cross design and backcross to P1 parent which would be the recurrent parent.

After the crossing, we got a lot of BC1F1 individuals and we might select one suitable individual with some criteria such as the highest recurrent parent genome recovery, and backcross to the recurrent parent to generate BC2F1 population.

>From the BC2F1 population which we assume 200 individuals in this population, and we keep selfing each individual for three generation.

Then we get BC2F4 population for your experiment.

I don’t know if I’m correct or not for the definition for the experimental design you asked.

The expected genotype frequency and the way to estimate the recombination fraction may different from F2 population in BC2F4.

So I don’t know if R/qtl can still work under this situation.

But the "Genetic map construction with R/qtl" still provide lots of way to try to clean up your genotype data.

And just like what Karl replied!

While the genetic distance is too large between two markers, it means these two markers are acting like they are independent to each other.

If these two markers are close to each other in physical map and they still have large genetic distance, there might have some quality issue in your genotype table.

Go through the "Genetic map construction with R/qtl” step-by-step with your genotype table would truly help you find out something in it! The guild line will still helpful for sure.

I hope my explanation will help a little.

Samuel

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Interpretation of "Plot of the LOD scores against the estimated recombination fractions"
messages.body_plain:
I would guess that you have largely complete genotype data, except that one set of markers is completely missing genotypes on a set of individuals.
For a pair of markers with the larger amount of genotype data, there's a functional relationship between the estimated recombination fraction and the LOD scores.
For a pair of markers where one or the other or both has the smaller amount of genotype data, there's also a functional relationship between rec frac and LOD, but with a given rec frac corresponding to a smaller LOD score.

karl

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I have some confusion over the use of the formula option in addqtl(). I'm hoping someone can shine a light for me here.
For some reason, I assume by not providing an explicit formula to addqtl, it by default uses the qtl object (provided as input option) as an additive covariate and searches for any additional additive QTL. Basically, i'm thinking the following calls are equivalent

#We make a qtl object with one qtl
qtl1 <- makeqtl(args)
#Then the following two calls should be equivalent
addqtl(cross, qtl=qtl1, formula=y~Q1+Q2)
addqtl(cross, qtl=qtl1)

This could be an incorrect assumption but any light on this would be helpful. Specifically, I have genotypes (~8000 on 384 individuals) called using the MSG (Andolfatto et al 2011) pipeline for a Backcross. I read these into R (3.4.4) using David Sterns read.cross.msg (https://github.com/dstern/read_cross_msg/blob/master/read.cross.msg.1.5.R) function. messages.body_plain:
The "f2" cross type in R/qtl is for an intercross between two inbred lines. The genotypes are to be coded like, say, "A" being homozygous for one inbred founder and "B" for the other, and "H" for heterozygotes. And where the "allele switching" occurs is when the "A" and "B" genotypes are backwards for a marker.

You mention "wild and F1 individuals" which suggests maybe you're considering a cross between outbred individuals? The "F2" cross type is not appropriate for this case.

It's potentially possible to use the "4way" cross type for crosses between outbred individuals, but it's neither easy nor documented, and you need to first infer the haplotypes in the F1 parents, and R/qtl includes no tools for this.

karl

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Inputting a mapping data from another mapping program (JoinMap) in R/qtl
messages.body_plain:
You need to provide more information: type of cross, numbers of chromosomes and markers, nature of the differences between the maps.

read.cross can read some JoinMap/MapQTL files, format="mapqtl". Here are the details from the help for read.cross:

> MapQTL format
>
> This format requires three files, described in the manual of the MapQTL program (same as JoinMap).
>
> genfile corresponds to the loc file containing the genotype data. Each marker and its genotypes should be on a single line.
>
> mapfile corresponds to the map file containing the linkage group assignment, marker names and their map positions.
>
> phefile corresponds to the qua file containing the phenotypes.
>
> For the moment, only 4-way crosses are supported (CP population type in MapQTL).

But if you already have a file in R/qtl format, I would try to insert the map from the JoinMap file into that file.

karl

messages.body_plain:
Dr. Broman,

I am analyzing a F2 intercross between two inbred lines of Drosophila (athabasca and mahican). We have 5 chromosomes, and there are a total of 499 markers.

In R/qtl, markers on chromosome 2 split into two linkage groups, and markers on chr3 & 4 were all in one linkage group. In Joinmap, chr3 and chr X were in one linkage group. Also, the order of the markers are not the same between the two programs.

In terms of using the map file from Joinmap into R/qtl, is there any documentation/help on how to insert the amp from the JoinMap file into R/qtl format file?

Thank you so much for your help!
